BUS.G11.T3.ENTRE.A1.title: Entrepreneurial qualities & success factors
BUS.G11.T3.ENTRE.A1.description: Assessing the degree to which a business embraces entrepreneurial qualities (risk-taking, perseverance, good management) and critically reflecting on a venture to identify its key success factors (sustainability, profitability, customer base) and areas for improvement.
BUS.G11.T3.ENTRE.A1.strand: T3 — Entrepreneurial success, citizenship, marketing & production functions
BUS.G11.T3.ENTRE.A1.recovery_strategy: Entrepreneurial qualities are personal characteristics (risk-taking, perseverance, good management, vision). Key success factors are what makes a business work: a loyal customer base, profitability and sustainability. Judge a venture against these, then name areas to improve.

questions.question: Which of these is an entrepreneurial quality?
options: Giving up at the first problem
questions.memo: Risk-taking is a key entrepreneurial quality — the willingness to take calculated chances to pursue an opportunity.

questions.question: A key success factor for a business is a loyal _________ base.
questions.memo: A loyal customer base brings repeat sales and is one of the main factors behind a successful business.

questions.question: True or false: Profitability is one of the key success factors of a business.
questions.memo: A business must make a profit to survive and grow, so profitability is a key success factor.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT an entrepreneurial quality?
options: Giving up easily when things get hard
questions.expected: Giving up easily when things get hard
questions.memo: Giving up easily is the opposite of perseverance. The others — perseverance, confidence and vision — are entrepreneurial qualities.

questions.question: _________ means the business is able to keep operating successfully into the future.
questions.memo: Sustainability is the ability of a business to keep going and remain viable over the long term.

questions.question: True or false: Perseverance means continuing to work towards a goal despite setbacks.
questions.memo: Perseverance is pushing on towards a goal even when problems and setbacks arise — a core entrepreneurial quality.

questions.question: Sort each item into whether it is an entrepreneurial quality or not.
questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Perseverance, vision, good management and confidence are entrepreneurial qualities; fearing all risk and refusing to adapt are not.

questions.question: How do you assess whether a business embraces entrepreneurial qualities?
options: Check whether it shows risk-taking, perseverance, good management and vision
Count how many staff it has only
Look only at the colour of its logo
Check whether the owner is tall
questions.expected: Check whether it shows risk-taking, perseverance, good management and vision
questions.memo: You judge a business against the entrepreneurial qualities — does it take sensible risks, persevere, manage well and have a clear vision?

questions.question: Which of these is a key success factor of a business?
questions.memo: A loyal, growing customer base is a key success factor; the other options are problems, not strengths.

questions.question: Thesis: 'A business should regularly identify its areas for improvement.' Choose the THREE strongest supporting reasons.
questions.thesis: A business should regularly identify its areas for improvement.

pool.text: It helps the business fix weaknesses before they become serious
It keeps the business competitive as the market changes
It guides where to focus effort and resources
Identifying weaknesses always bankrupts a business
The owner enjoys filling in forms
A business is already perfect and never needs to improve

questions.memo: The strong reasons are fixing weaknesses early, staying competitive, and focusing effort. The others are false or irrelevant.

questions.question: An area for _________ is a weakness the business should work on.
questions.memo: An area for improvement is a weak point that, if addressed, would make the business stronger.

questions.question: True or false: A business with no customers at all can still be considered successful.
questions.memo: Without customers there are no sales and no income, so a business cannot be successful without a customer base.

questions.question: Sort each item into whether it is a success factor or an area for improvement for a struggling shop.

items.text: Weak marketing that few people see

questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Loyal customers, healthy profit and a trusted brand are success factors; poor stock control, slow service and weak marketing are areas to improve.

questions.question: Why is it useful for a business to identify its areas for improvement?
options: So it can fix weaknesses, grow and stay competitive
So it can ignore all its problems
So it can stop serving customers
So it can avoid making any changes
questions.expected: So it can fix weaknesses, grow and stay competitive
questions.memo: Identifying weak points lets a business improve, grow and keep up with competitors.

questions.question: A business changes its products quickly when customer tastes shift. Which entrepreneurial quality does this show?
questions.memo: Adapting quickly to change shows flexibility, an important entrepreneurial quality.

questions.question: Good _________ and leadership is one of the entrepreneurial qualities.
questions.memo: Good management and leadership — planning, organising and guiding others — is a recognised entrepreneurial quality.

questions.question: A café makes a profit but its only chef is overworked and about to quit. Which area for improvement is most urgent for its sustainability?
options: Reducing reliance on one person by training or hiring more staff
Changing the colour of the menus
Ignoring the problem because it is profitable now
questions.expected: Reducing reliance on one person by training or hiring more staff
questions.memo: Depending on a single overworked chef threatens future operations, so spreading that capacity is the key improvement for sustainability.

questions.question: Which situation most threatens a business's long-term sustainability?
options: Losing customers steadily with no plan to win new ones
Earning a small but steady profit
questions.expected: Losing customers steadily with no plan to win new ones
questions.memo: A shrinking customer base with no plan to replace it undermines future income and threatens the business's survival.

questions.question: Why is a loyal customer base so valuable as a success factor?
options: Repeat customers provide steady income and often recommend the business
Loyal customers never need to be served
It means the business can ignore quality
It removes the need to make a profit
questions.expected: Repeat customers provide steady income and often recommend the business
questions.memo: Loyal customers buy again and refer others, giving the business reliable income and free word-of-mouth marketing.

questions.question: An entrepreneur reflects on her venture. Which approach best combines assessing qualities with finding improvements?
options: Judge the business against entrepreneurial qualities and success factors, then list specific things to improve
Assume everything is fine and change nothing
Only count the cash and ignore everything else
questions.expected: Judge the business against entrepreneurial qualities and success factors, then list specific things to improve
questions.memo: A useful reflection measures the venture against the qualities and success factors, then turns the gaps into concrete areas for improvement.
